overview: This bill changes two rules at the Board of Veterans' Appeals, the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs that decides appeals of veterans' benefit claims. First, when a veteran appeals the denial of a "supplemental claim" (a request to reopen a claim), the Board could no longer refuse to help solely because the veteran didn't submit new and relevant evidence. Second, when the Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims sends a case back to the Board, the Board would review the existing record plus any new evidence the veteran submits within 90 days. It also extends, to January 30, 2035, an existing limit on VA pension payments to certain veterans living in nursing homes paid for by Medicaid, which helps offset the bill's costs. As of October 21, 2025, a House committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar.
for: Supporters say the bill keeps veterans from losing appeals on a technicality and gives them a clear window to add evidence when a court sends their case back.
against: Critics say letting more cases move forward without new evidence and adding evidence after a court remand could add to the Board's workload and slow decisions for other veterans, and that the pension limit used to offset costs affects low-income veterans in nursing homes.
